g.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Six NGED solar farms, daylight hours, September 2019 to June 2026. ERA5: ECMWF's reanalysis of past weather. CAMS: satellite irradiance service. The XGBoost model predicts a 10 to 90% interval that should hold 80% of outcomes. Circle: that predicted interval. Diamond: one fixed-width interval, from the same variable set's errors, that holds the same share of outcomes as the circle. A narrower interval at the same share is better, so a set that helps with uncertainty sits left of its diamond. A variable set is the list of inputs the XGBoost model is given. G0: sun position, ERA5 solar radiation (ssrd), and air temperature (t2m). Each group adds to the one before. G1: total cloud cover. G2: low, mid, and high cloud cover. G3: clear-sky radiation. G4: cloud water and cloud base height. G5: direct beam. G6: wind and thermal radiation. G7: humidity and haze. G8: snow and albedo. G9 (the full set): all other ERA5 variables. G10: G9 plus CAMS aerosol. Negative control: G2 plus shuffled copies of the other variables, which carry no information. MARS-only: 12 ERA5 variables that neither ECMWF's free forecast feed nor Open-Meteo serves. Main XGBoost tuning setting only. Exploratory: not named in the study plan before any result existed, and not corrected for multiple comparisons.'

text.font-family: Matter XH, DM Sans, sans-serif
